thread.title: Apple working on ‘Netflix for games,’ report says

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Apple working on ‘Netflix for games,’ report says
text: Jan 28, 2019, 2:18pm EST Apple Inc. is exploring the idea of launching a subscription service for games. The platform would work like a ‘Netflix for games,’ charging a flat fee for access to a library of titles. Cheddar first reported the news, citing five anonymous sources. The move would come as Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) is facing declining hardware sales. The computer giant revised its first-quarter guidance at the start of the year to reflect $5 billion less revenue due to slower-than-expected holiday iPhone sales. A gaming subscription would be one of several services the company is developing to beef up that side of the business, including a video streaming service a la Netflix. Apple has committed an initial $1 billion to content for that initiative, which has signed deals with “Parenthood” showrunner Jason Katims, Justin Lin (several “Fast & Furious” movies and “Star Trek: Beyond”), Oprah Winfrey, Sesame Workshop and Peanuts, and is working on series including “Amazing Stories,” a drama about a morning new show starring Jennifer Aniston, Reese Witherspoon and Steve Carell, and a thriller from M. Night Shyamalan, among other projects. Apple announces its first-quarter earnings on Tuesday. The company started talking about the idea for a game subscription service with developers in the latter half of last year, reported Cheddar. Apple has also considered becoming a publisher in partnership with game developers, which would see the company handling distribution, marketing and other aspects of game publishing. It’s unclear how much such a subscription would cost or what games would be available on the platform, and the service is still in the early stages and could never come to pass. Apple isn’t the only one to explore this idea: Sony’s PlayStation and Microsoft’s Xbox both offer similar subscriptions, with Amazon and Google also working on similar services.
